report.summary: All tagged claims check out against the cited DRHP excerpts; I found no unsupported or wrong-source tags. The only citation gaps are the un-tagged assertions that the filing does not disclose whether the offer is a fresh issue or an offer for sale, plus one un-tagged business-model summary that could re-use the existing tender-process citation. These are process flags rather than factual contradictions, so the underlying sourcing is sound.

untagged_claims.sentence: The extracted pages do not say whether the 44,28,000 shares are entirely a fresh issue — new shares sold by the company, with the money going to it — or include an offer for sale, where existing shareholders sell some of their holdings and take the proceeds themselves.
untagged_claims.suggestion: This material offer-structure absence claim needs a citation to the offer/issue-structure pages (e.g., drhp-p29) or should be cut.

untagged_claims.sentence: The extracted pages do not spell out whether the 44,28,000 shares are entirely a fresh issue or include an offer for sale. This matters because a fresh issue puts money into the company, while an offer for sale puts money into the pockets of selling shareholders. The distinction is material to what the IPO is actually for.
untagged_claims.suggestion: Same as above; tag the absence claim to the issue/offer pages.

untagged_claims.sentence: There is no negotiated pipeline, no repeat-order book in the usual sense — every contract is a fresh competition.
